note: Answer key for the Chicago parcel kit, built from primary sources (City zoning layer, Zoning MapServer, Municipal Code text current through the Council Journal of 2026-06-17 (re-checked 2026-10-21 against the refresh from 2026-03-18: none of the Title 17 sections the refresh changed is one a keyed field cites, so no value moved), ordinance PDFs, Cook County Assessor). P1-P7 are the 2026-10-01 set; P8+ were added 2026-10-02 (`added`), with the same method, to cover downtown, manufacturing, lakefront and transit-served cases the first seven do not. NOT yet reviewed by a Chicago zoning professional: P2, P3 and P6 are the most interpretive, and so are P9 and P12 (transit-served-location rules). Overlay truth comes from the same City service UrbanLayer queries, so overlay scores are not independent.
prompt_template: I'm evaluating the property at {address} in Chicago, Illinois for a possible project. Tell me, with sources: (1) the zoning district currently in effect for this parcel; (2) {use}; (3) the key bulk and density standards that apply (FAR, max height, min lot area per dwelling unit, setbacks, as applicable); (4) any overlays or special designations that apply (Planned Development, landmark/historic district, transit-oriented or transit-served location, ADU area, ARO zone, special service area, special districts); (5) the parking requirement and any transit-related reduction; (6) {task} For each item cite the specific Municipal Code section or official source and tell me how I can verify it. Say how confident you are and what you could not determine.

parcels.use_question: Could I build a two-flat (two dwelling units) here?
parcels.task_question: Could I add a coach house / accessory dwelling unit on this lot?
parcels.why: Plain RS-2 baseline; ADU nuance (not in an ADU-allowed area)

A.basis: City zoning layer dj47-wfun at the Assessor centroid; 17-2-0100

B.answer: Two-flat NOT allowed (use table 17-2-0207: detached house P; two-flat '-' in RS1/RS2)

numbers.name: mla
numbers.basis: 17-2-0301-A, 17-2-0303-A (lot area per unit = min lot area in RS-2)

D.basis: City Zoning MapServer layers 2-24 at the centroid

F.answer: Coach house NOT allowed (no ADU zone, layer 17; 17-7-0574)

parcels.use_question: Is a multi-unit residential building (3+ units) permitted by right? (This is a vacant lot of roughly 3,150 square feet.)
parcels.task_question: What is the maximum number of dwelling units I could build by right on this lot, and could I build 6 units?
parcels.why: Vacant infill lot; geocoder trap (address interpolates into adjacent RS-3); MLA arithmetic (4 not 6)

A.basis: Ordinance A7210; the Census-geocoded address point falls in an adjacent RS-3 polygon

wrong: (multi-?unit|3\+|(3|three) or more)[^.\n]{0,80}(not permitted|not allowed|prohibited|not by right)

D.basis: 606 district (layer 9; does NOT change RM-4.5 density per 17-7-0591); ARO CPA (layer 20)

F.answer: 4 units (3,154 / 700 = 4.5 -> 4); 6 is not achievable by right

resolution.note: a vacant lot: no Address Points row

parcels.use_question: Can I build apartments above ground-floor retail, and can I put apartments on the ground floor?
parcels.task_question: What are the maximum height and floor area ratio for a mixed-use building here, and does proximity to transit change what I can build (including any density or parking provisions)?
parcels.why: B1-2 near rail: TOD parking relief yes, TOD density bonus NO (dash-2); ground-floor dwelling needs special use

B.answer: Dwelling units above the ground floor: permitted; on the ground floor: special use (17-3-0102-D; 17-3-0103-A)

D.basis: TOD (CTA) layer; ARO CPA; SSA #31 Greater Ravenswood

E.answer: Parking reducible up to 100% (17-10-0102-B.1(a)); density bonuses only in dash-3/D-3 districts -> NOT at B1-2

F.answer: Height/FAR as in C; transit changes parking only, not density

resolution.note: Address Points names ...025, the Assessor names ...044

parcels.task_question: What is the maximum floor area ratio and building height allowed?
parcels.why: Planned Development: base-district numbers do not apply; standards live in the PD ordinance

B.answer: Governed by a PD, not a base district

resolution.note: a building PIN the Parcel Universe has no record for

parcels.use_question: Is ground-floor retail with apartments above allowed?
parcels.task_question: Could I demolish the existing building and build a new mixed-use building here? What approvals or restrictions apply?
parcels.why: Overlay stack incl. a Chicago Landmark district and a CHRS orange-rated building; geocoder trap (address interpolates into a C1-3 polygon)

A.basis: Ordinance 17230; the Census-geocoded address point falls in a C1-3 polygon (O2021-4070). Address spans 3 PINs, all B3-2

B.answer: Yes: B3 permits dwelling units above the ground floor (17-3-0104-C)

D.basis: Milwaukee Avenue Chicago Landmark district HD-56, designated 2008-04-09 (layer 6); National Register (layer 8); TOD (CTA); ARO Inclusionary; SSA #33 Wicker Park. NOT an individual Chicago Landmark: Noel State Bank is in layer 7, which holds the Chicago Historic Resources Survey's orange/red-rated buildings (9,298 records, most with no designation date), and is absent from the City's official Chicago Landmarks list (data portal tdab-kixi, 317 landmarks) and from layer 5 (landmark boundaries). Corrected 2026-10-02: the first key read layer 7 as 'individual landmarks'.

E.answer: Transit-served: parking reducible up to 100% (17-10-0102-B.1(a)); no added parking for reuse of a contributing building in a landmark district (17-10-0102-A.2)

F.answer: Not by right: the parcel is in the Milwaukee Avenue Chicago Landmark district, so a permit to alter, demolish or build needs written approval of the Commission on Chicago Landmarks (Municipal Code 2-120-740)

groups: Commission on Chicago Landmarks|written approval|2-120-740|Landmarks Commission

parcels.use_question: Could I build a two-flat here?
parcels.task_question: Could I add a coach house or other additional dwelling unit here, and under what conditions or limits?
parcels.why: RS-3 with the 606 Predominance-of-the-Block district (MLA 1,500) and a conditional ADU zone

B.answer: Two-flat PERMITTED in RS-3 (use table row 3); 606 district lowers MLA to 1,500 (17-2-0303-B.1)

D.basis: 606 district (layer 9); ADU Zone 10 (layer 17); ARO CPA; TOD (CTA)

F.answer: Allowed with limits: ADU Zone 10 -> (1) annual limit, (2) owner occupancy (17-7-0573/-0574)

parcels.use_question: Is residential use allowed on this parcel?
parcels.task_question: What is the zoning here, and has it changed recently?
parcels.why: Freshness: rezoned M1-2 -> RT-4 by an ordinance passed 2026-06-17 (open-data layer updated 2026-08-21)

A.basis: Ordinance O2026-0025358 (App. 23082T1), passed 2026-06-17; the address point lands in an adjacent RT-4 polygon (O2018-3982)

B.answer: Yes: RT-4 permits two-flat, townhouse and multi-unit residential (17-2-0207)

F.answer: Yes: rezoned M1-2 -> RT-4 in June 2026

parcels.use_question: Can I build apartments above ground-floor office or retail space, and can I put apartments on the ground floor?
parcels.task_question: What is the maximum floor area ratio and building height allowed here, and can the floor area ratio be exceeded?
parcels.why: Downtown DC-16: base FAR 16 with bonuses, no height cap but a Planned Development height threshold, and its own use table (ground-floor dwellings are a special use)

B.answer: Dwelling units above the ground floor: permitted; multi-unit on the ground floor: special use (use table 17-4-0207, rows 3 and 4: DC 'P' above, 'S' on the ground floor)

F.answer: Base FAR 16.0 (17-4-0405-A) with bonus floor area available (17-4-0405-B, 17-4-1000); no maximum building height (17-4-0407), but Planned Development approval is required at 440 ft or more (residential) and 600 ft or more (nonresidential) (17-8-0512-B)

parcels.use_question: Is ground-floor retail with apartments above allowed, and what minimum lot area per dwelling unit applies?
parcels.task_question: Does being near transit let me build more than the base standards here, and by what process?
parcels.why: B3-3 inside the transit-served-location distances: the positive case. Density, FAR and height increases exist at dash-3 but only through a Type I map amendment, a PD or an ARO entitlement, not by right

B.answer: Yes: dwelling units above the ground floor are permitted in B3 (use table 17-3-0207, row 3)

numbers.name: height_ft
numbers.basis: 17-3-0408-A (dash 3: 50/55/65/65 with compliant ground-floor commercial; 50/50/60/60 without, by lot frontage)

D.basis: TOD (CTA); ARO; SSA Albany Park (observed from the City layers 2026-10-02)

E.answer: Parking reducible up to 100% in a transit-served location (17-10-0102-B.1(a))

F.answer: Yes, but not by right: in a B3 district within 2,640 ft of a rail station or 1,320 ft of a bus corridor, reduced lot area per unit, higher FAR (3.5 to 4.0 with ARO units) and added height are allowed only through a Type I zoning map amendment, a Planned Development, or an ARO entitlement (17-3-0402-B, 17-3-0403-B, 17-3-0408-B)

parcels.use_question: Could I build apartments here (new residential or a conversion)?
parcels.task_question: What would it take to put housing on this parcel?
parcels.why: M2-3 manufacturing district: residential is not a listed use and unlisted uses are prohibited, so a use-allowed lookup must say no

B.answer: No: household living is not in the M-district use table (17-5-0207) and uses not listed are prohibited (17-5-0204)

D.basis: TOD (CTA); ARO (observed from the City layers 2026-10-02)

F.answer: Not by right: it needs a zoning map amendment to a district that allows residential (Type I, 17-13-0302) or a Planned Development (17-13-0600)

parcels.use_question: Is a multi-unit residential building permitted by right?
parcels.task_question: What review beyond the zoning district's standards applies to a new building on this parcel?
parcels.why: RM-6.5 inside the Lakefront Protection District: no height cap but a PD threshold, a separate ordinance (Chapter 16-4), and a CHRS orange-rated building that is NOT a designated landmark

B.answer: Yes: multi-unit (3+ units) residential is permitted in RM-6.5 (use table 17-2-0207, row 5)

wrong: (multi-?unit|3\+|(3|three) or more)[^.\n]{0,80}(not permitted|not allowed|prohibited|not by right)

D.basis: Lakefront Protection District (Private Lakefront, layer 3); ARO; National Register individual property 'The Cornelia' (layer 8). A CHRS orange-rated building (layer 7) but NOT a designated Chicago Landmark: absent from layer 5 and from the official landmarks list (tdab-kixi). Observed from the City layers 2026-10-02

F.answer: All development in the Lake Michigan and Chicago Lakefront Protection District is subject to Chapter 16-4, the Lakefront Protection Ordinance (17-6-0204-B), in addition to the zoning standards; a building of 140 ft or more also needs Planned Development approval in RM-6.5 (17-8-0512-A)

parcels.use_question: Can I build apartments above ground-floor retail, and what minimum lot area per dwelling unit applies?
parcels.task_question: Does being near transit let me build more density here than the base standards?

B.answer: Yes: dwelling units above the ground floor are permitted in C2 (use table 17-3-0207, row 3)

numbers.name: height_ft
numbers.basis: 17-3-0408-A (dash 5: 50/55/70/80 with compliant ground-floor commercial; 50/50/65/75 without, by lot frontage; more than the 100-ft-lot height only by PD)

D.basis: TOD (CTA); ARO (observed from the City layers 2026-10-02)

E.answer: Parking reducible up to 100% in a transit-served location (17-10-0102-B.1(a))

resolution_note: Resolution expectations were observed from the county's Address Points and Assessor Parcel Addresses datasets on 2026-10-02; they test that the Profile reports what those records say, not independent ground truth.

corrections.now: Milwaukee Avenue landmark district only; orange-rated in the historic-resources survey, not individually designated
corrections.why: The first key read the zoning map's 'Landmark Buildings' layer (layer 7) as designations. It holds the survey's 9,298 orange/red-rated buildings, most with no designation date. The City's landmark-boundary layer (layer 5) and the official Chicago Landmarks list (data portal tdab-kixi, 317 landmarks) have no entry for the building. Found while keying P11, where the product and the key disagreed.
corrections.effect: UrbanLayer's Profile and chat both claimed an individual landmark on this parcel; with the corrected key that is now a confident-wrong overlay, and it is a product defect (see the plan, F8).

corrections.why: WS1 M2 (#65) replaced the bare vintage note with code_currency (vintage plus the amendments passed since) whenever the amendment data is present, which on prod is always. Product id change, not a law change.
corrections.effect: The coverage panel had reported 0/12 parcels with exactly their notes since #65; with the id updated it measures what it was meant to.
